concept: Engram row prefetch overlapped with preceding transformer blocks in Mac runtimes
summary: ds4 V4.1 prefill starts a reader pthread per Engram table that reads rows through `ds4_engram_read_batch` in 2,048-token chunks and publishes a completed-row counter with release semantics.

facts.text: ds4 V4.1 prefill starts a reader pthread per Engram table that reads rows through `ds4_engram_read_batch` in 2,048-token chunks and publishes a completed-row counter with release semantics.
The prefill consumer waits on that counter, polling with a 1 ms nanosleep, so a chunk's Engram layer can start before later chunks have been read.
ds4 enables the Engram overlap only when the prompt has at least 1,024 tokens, and offers environment switches to disable the prefetch, the pipelined wait, or the batched read.

ds4 V4.1 Engram layers are indices 1 and 14; table 0's prefetch starts before the layer loop and table 1's starts at layer 2, with a code comment saying it fills the buffer for layer 14 while the intervening encoder layers run.
Both prefetch starts write to the same `engram_prefetch` GPU-visible buffer.
ds4's decode step (`ds41_graph_step`) reads both tables' rows synchronously with `ds4_engram_read_batch` before it begins the GPU command buffer on Apple platforms.
ds4's Qwen n-gram path reads each 256-token chunk's rows synchronously, sorted by row id, with up to 16 readers via `dispatch_apply_f`, before the forward pass.
ds4's Engram constants are 2 layers, n-gram size 4, 8 heads, 24 columns per token per layer, 256 dimensions and 264 bytes per row.
`ds4_engram_hash` builds, for each of n-gram orders 2 to 4, 8 head ids per token per layer from a multiplicative hash modulo per-head primes, so 24 row ids per token per layer.
The V4.1 GGUF metadata in ds4 names Engram row counts 384,006,168 and 384,016,682, the encoding `e4m3_e8m0_32_row264` and a compressed vocabulary of 99,092.
One ds4 decode token issues 2 tables times 24 rows = 48 random 264-byte reads (12,672 bytes) before deduplication.
The two V4.1 tables total about 769 million rows times 264 bytes, roughly 189 GiB, which matches the 189 GiB of Engram tables in ds4's model documentation.
The paper's prefetch window is the compute of the blocks before the Engram layer, and the paper places the module at specific layers to use that buffer.
llama.cpp PR 27794 has a reviewer remark that qwen4 gives n-grams to the second layer, not the first, which can hide the lazy read.
A downstream fork's note on PR 27794 states upstream's own commit measured MADV_RANDOM without batched row prefetch at 94.4 s, an untouched mapping at 36.7 s, and MADV_RANDOM plus prefetch at 34.1 s.

The same fork measured its lazy-read default at pp512 352 tok/s versus 99 tok/s with lazy reading off, and tg128 33.4 versus 26.1 tok/s, on an AMD gfx1151 machine with a 95 GiB table and 62 GB RAM; the numbers are not Apple Silicon.
No source found overlaps Engram or n-gram reads with preceding blocks during decode on a Mac, and none reports a per-token stall for it.
